newsitem.title: PERU: Jesuit who stayed with hostages to celebrate Mass.
newsitem.headline: Jesuit who stayed with hostages to celebrate Mass.

text.p: A Roman Catholic priest who turned down his chance of freedom will celebrate a Christmas Mass for the hostages held for a week by Marxist guerrillas in the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima on Tuesday night.

A Red Cross volunteer said the Rev. Juan Julio Wicht would hand out sacraments and offer a message of hope to the 105 hostages still being held by rebels of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA).
Wicht, a Jesuit who teaches at Peru's University of the Pacific, turned down a chance to walk free along with 225 hostages released by the gunmen on Sunday night.
"I prefer to stay to help the hostages spiritually. I don't have any family," he said, according to one of the captives freed that night.

Wicht has led prayer sessions every morning in a small room on the first floor of the residency since the second day of the seven-day siege. Some rebels watched the services but did not participate, the former hostage said.
Wicht also celebrated a full-scale Mass on the stairs of the residence on Sunday, and many of the 330-plus hostages at the time took Communion, witnesses said.

"In his Masses, the priest called for calm and a prompt solution to the problem, which has prevented many people from spending Christmas with their families," said another former hostage who asked not to be named.
The freed man added that Wicht was well respected by the rebels, who allowed him to move freely about the two floors of the building talking to the hostages.
Earlier on Tuesday, Miguel Irizar, bishop of Lima's neighbouring port of Callao, called for "love and union" between the hostages and their captors.
"Let's hope that (the guerrillas) are touched by the Lord this Christmas and allow all the hostages to go free," Irizar said.
